prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on your goals (realistic talking-head ads, animated/product ads, repurposing long videos, scale and A/B testing, budget, platform). Below are the best options by use case plus a quick decision guide so you can pick the one that fits you.

Top choices (strengths & when to use)

- Synthesia
  - Strengths: very good, realistic AI presenters (avatars), many languages, fast script → talking-head video.
  - Best for: product demos/testimonials or localized ads using virtual spokespeople; teams that want consistent brand presenters.
- HeyGen / Elai.io / Colossyan
  - Strengths: similar to Synthesia — text-to-video with AI actors; simpler pricing/UX on some platforms.
  - Best for: alternative avatar solutions; use if you prefer different voices/looks or pricing.
- Runway
  - Strengths: powerful generative video models and creative editing tools for more novel visuals (background replacement, inpainting, generative edits).
  - Best for: high-creative ads, unique visuals, editors who want creative control.
- Pictory
  - Strengths: excellent at turning long-form content (webinars/podcasts/blogs) into short social ads, auto-subtitles and caption styling.
  - Best for: repurposing existing long videos into many short ad variants.
- Descript
  - Strengths: text-based video editing, Overdub (voice cloning), excellent for fast edits and captions.
  - Best for: creator-driven ads and voice edits where you need precise control and speed.
- InVideo / Lumen5 / Promo.com / Biteable / VEED
  - Strengths: template libraries, easy editors, auto-resize for ad platforms, stock media.
  - Best for: rapid production of platform-ready ads (Facebook/Instagram/TikTok) with minimal learning curve.
- Shakr / VidMob
  - Strengths: built for ad-scale and performance optimization. Shakr has templates engineered for social ad performance; VidMob adds creative analytics and optimization.
  - Best for: agencies and e-commerce teams that need to produce and test hundreds of ad variants and optimize for performance.

How to choose
1. Define your primary goal: realistic presenter? animated product spot? repurposing content? scale and testing?
2. Consider output needs: resolution, aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), platform integrations (Facebook, TikTok, Google), and languages.
3. Budget and scale: avatar tools (Synthesia/HeyGen) tend to be subscription/enterprise; template tools (InVideo/Lumen5) are cheaper; scale platforms (Shakr/VidMob) are enterprise-level.
4. Try before you commit: use trials to evaluate quality, turnaround, voice/naturalness, and how easy it is to create A/B variants.
5. Measure results: pick a tool that lets you iterate fast — faster iterations → better ad optimization.

If you tell me:
- your primary channel(s) (TikTok, FB, Google, YouTube),
- whether you want live-looking presenters vs animated/stock,
- your monthly budget,
I’ll recommend the top 2–3 tools and one sample workflow (script → production → scale) tailored to your needs.
